passages.original: 586, Juvenalis Anastasio ann. 457. Nicephorus fluxisse tradit quatuor et septuaginta. Hoc primum peccatum. Joanni tribuit annos omnino quindecim cum triginta sederit , defunctus enim est anno 417, ut ex Augustini Zosimique literis apertum est, et Cyrillo successit, cujus mortem contigisse anno 8 Theodosii M., id est ann. 386, tradit Hieronymus, cap. 19 de Scriptoribus ecclesiasticis. Istud secundum. Tertium longe mirabilius, si non absurdius, tribuit Praylio, qui Joanni successit, annos viginti, quo pacto sedisse dici debet ad annum usque 456 aut 457.
passages.english: 586, [and] Juvenal [gave way] to Anastasius in the year 457. Nicephorus records that seventy-four [years] elapsed. This is the first error. He assigns to John fifteen years in all, although he sat for thirty; for he died in the year 417, as is clear from the letters of Augustine and Zosimus, and he succeeded Cyril, whose death Jerome, in chapter 19 of On Ecclesiastical Writers, records as having occurred in the eighth year of Theodosius the Great, that is, in the year 386. That is the second. The third, far more astonishing, if not more absurd: he assigns to Praylius, who succeeded John, twenty years, by which reckoning he must be said to have sat right up to the year 456 or 457.
passages.notes: The passage opens mid-sentence: the preceding context ends 'siquidem Cyrillus decessit Joanni ann.', so '586' completes that clause (Cyril gave way to John in the year [3]86?). The figure 586 as printed is presumably a scanning or printing error for 386, which the passage itself gives as the date of Cyril's death; translated as it stands. The verb for Juvenal and Anastasius is supplied from the parallel construction ('decessit').
